subject: maths
question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a train crossing two objects in the **same direction**:

**Speed of Train (V)** = (S₂ × T₂ − S₁ × T₁) ÷ (T₂ − T₁)

V = (6 × 14 − 4 × 12) ÷ (14 − 12)

V = (84 − 48) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of person 1 (v₁) = 4 km/h | Time (t₁) = 12 s

Speed of person 2 (v₂) = 6 km/h | Time (t₂) = 14 s

Let the **speed of the train** be V km/h and the **length of the train** be L meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/980714f6d83c72578a6e15f993652599f4cfbd2d17453309f83743076de0b888.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Length of train (L) is constant in both cases.

⇒ L = (V − 4) × (5/18) × 12 — (i)

⇒ L = (V − 6) × (5/18) × 14 — (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ (V − 4) × 12 = (V − 6) × 14

⇒ 12V − 48 = 14V − 84

⇒ 14V − 12V = 84 − 48

⇒ 2V = 36

⇒ V = 18 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = V₁ − V₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, person, or tree, the distance covered is exactly equal to the **length of the train**.</p
